brief.headline: Carlyle to acquire $7.7bn consumer loan portfolio from Truist
bullets: M&A & Buyouts: Carlyle has agreed to acquire a $7.7bn (£5.8bn) portfolio of unsecured personal loans from US bank Truist as it expands its asset-backed finance (ABF) business.

Private Credit: Goldman Sachs has entered into a strategic partnership with Israeli asset manager Phoenix Financial, which plans to deploy more than $4bn (£3bn) across global private credit opportunities.
Earnings & AUM: The idea that the AI trade has been mostly immune to rising bond yields isn’t quite right, one strategist notes.
M&A & Buyouts: This week’s largest control transactions were private-equity deals in everything but the label on the capital.
Investor Outlook: Barry speaks with Bob Michele, CIO and Head of Global Fixed Income, Currency, and Commodities at JPMorgan.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,659.44 (down 1.1% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 16.5, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10% (down 9 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.35 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.23%, near long-run norms (down 2 bps on the prior reading).
